open_points.subject: State 2 time policy
open_points.text: instants Registry records and the 03:00 of A18 are UTC wall-clock time.
open_points.question: Which clock authority supplies every recorded instant, what exact aware-UTC representation and precision is used, and does one operation take one shared reading for all timestamps and date comparisons or a separate reading for each field and check?
options: Inject one UTC clock authority and take one reading per operation, reused for its records, audit entry and date checks
Read the operating-system wall clock separately for each check and written field
Declare different clock authorities or reading counts per operation
open_points.default_guess: Use an injected aware-UTC clock and one reading per operation, except where A18 explicitly requires a later reading for another step.

witness.initial: A project is at revision 3 and the UTC wall clock is about to cross midnight.
events: The owner submits a correction that also writes an audit entry.
One implementation reads the project last-changed instant before midnight and the audit instant after midnight; another takes one reading and uses it for both.
outcomes: The project and its audit entry carry different instants and may fall on different UTC dates.
The project and its audit entry carry the same instant and UTC date.
witness.observer: The owner comparing the project card with the audit log

open_points.subject: A15 erase audit entries before a date
open_points.text: The date of an erasure is a date not later than today, the current date in UTC; a later date is refused.
open_points.question: At what single instant is “today” fixed for an erasure, and must that same reading supply the erasure entry's current instant?
options: Fix one UTC reading when the operation begins and derive both today and the entry instant from it
Read today during validation and read the entry instant separately when writing
Fix the time only after locks and the transaction have been acquired
open_points.default_guess: Take one UTC reading after acquiring the operation's locks and transaction and reuse it for validation and the entry.

witness.initial: The UTC time is immediately before midnight and the owner submits an erasure whose date is the next UTC date.
events: One implementation validates before midnight and reads the entry instant after midnight.
Another implementation fixes its operation time after midnight and uses it for both checks.
outcomes: The erasure is refused because its date is later than today.
The erasure is accepted because its date is today.

open_points.subject: M12 AuditSequence restoration semantics
open_points.text:
A store restored after a loss begins its own history from the backup's last number (R0-89).

A restored store holds this record as the backup holds it, the same record continued; Registry neither knows nor records that the store was restored.
open_points.question: Does restoration create a new store history with a new AuditSequence initialized from the backed-up number, or continue the identity of the backed-up AuditSequence record?
options: A new store history has its own AuditSequence initialized to the backed-up last number
The restored store continues the same AuditSequence entity and history
The record is copied but receives a new identity derived from the restored store
open_points.default_guess: Treat the restored store as a new history with a new store-scoped AuditSequence initialized to the backed-up value.

open_points.subject: A22 artifact vocabulary changes
open_points.text: What a change of it does to existing pointers is State 2's (A22).
open_points.question: Where is A22, and what happens to existing pointers, reads, retries, imports and new publications when a release removes or changes an artifact type or its owner service?
options: Grandfather existing pointers as readable history but refuse new publications and retries whose type was removed
Refuse startup while stored pointers use a removed or changed type
Migrate or rewrite existing pointers during the release
open_points.default_guess: Grandfather existing pointers unchanged and readable, while refusing new publications and retries under a removed type.

open_points.subject: A16 import alias validation
open_points.text: Any conflict — a project, room or pointer id production holds — or any malformed record of the picks refuses the whole import, and nothing changes (R0-50, R0-79).
open_points.question: Must confirmation refuse an owner-supplied imported-project alias longer than the M01 limit of 40 Unicode code points, and is that condition part of A16's malformed/missing-value recheck?
options: Refuse the whole import at mapping and confirmation when any supplied alias exceeds 40 code points
Accept the import because A16's listed malformed conditions do not include alias length
Truncate the alias to 40 code points
open_points.default_guess: Refuse the whole import without truncation.

witness.initial: A readable, otherwise valid export contains one picked project and has no conflicts.
events: The owner supplies a 41-code-point alias in the mapping and confirms it.
One implementation applies M01's refusal rule; another implements only A16's listed malformed and missing-value conditions.
outcomes: The import is refused and nothing changes.
The import commits with the 41-code-point alias.

open_points.subject: A16 imported object validation
open_points.text: A brought-in record is malformed when: a required value is missing (A02); it names a project or room the file does not hold; an id occurs twice among the file's records of one kind; a status is outside its vocabulary, or a pointer is `withdrawn` (v1 never withdrew one, M05); a pointer's type is not declared or its owner service is not the type's (A22); the versions of a project's pointers of one type are not 1..n, or are not every one `superseded` but the highest, which is `published`; an instant cannot be read; an `active` project has an archived instant or an `archived` one has none; a `superseded` pointer has no superseded instant or a `published` one has one; a record's own instant of change, archiving or supersession is before its own instant of creation, adding or publishing.
open_points.question: Are the newly declared Object constraints—kind in the four-member vocabulary, positive floor area, room count at least 1, and integral room count and floor—also import-malformation conditions, and at which checks are they shown and rechecked?
options: Treat every violation as malformed, show it in the mapping and refuse confirmation
Accept such values because A16's malformed list omits them
Drop invalid optional characteristics while importing
open_points.default_guess: Treat each violation as malformed and refuse the whole import.

open_points.subject: A15 AuditSequence atomicity
open_points.text: changes that write an entry are applied one at a time, and each entry takes the number after the last that history ever wrote, kept in the store apart from the entries (M12 AuditSequence), so an erasure does not lower it.
open_points.question: Which Required tests item must show that an append and the M12 update are atomic, that a failed append advances neither, and that concurrent ordinary appends—not only the append after an erasure—never reuse or duplicate a number?
options: Add a failure-and-concurrency test that inspects both entries and M12
Treat Required test 4 as sufficient even though it covers only the entry following an erasure
open_points.default_guess: Add an explicit atomicity and concurrent-append test.

open_points.subject: A17 new-store invariant
open_points.text: When the store's configured file does not exist and its directory does, Registry makes a new, empty store of the running release's version there at the start — no record but its audit sequence at 0 (M12)
open_points.question: Which Required tests item must show that a successfully created store contains exactly one M12 AuditSequence with value 0 and no other domain record, including after the temporary-file rename path?
options: Add a test that opens the completed new store and asserts the sole domain record is M12=0
Rely on the listener-failure cleanup test without inspecting the created store
open_points.default_guess: Add the explicit new-store contents test.

open_points.subject: A18 backup sequence metadata
open_points.text:
every kept backup is encrypted, consistent, checked, and records
  (instant, release, last sequence); no backup holds an agent session
open_points.question: Which Required tests item must show that the readable record contains the exact snapshot instant, release and M12 value, including 0 for a never-appended store, and that the integrity check compares the decrypted M12 value with that record?
options: Add a metadata test for both a new store and a store with erased audit entries
Treat the transaction-consistency test as implicitly covering metadata it does not mention
open_points.default_guess: Add an explicit metadata and M12-consistency test.

open_points.subject: A18 retention cutoff invariant
open_points.text:
after a run whose deletions succeeded: no backup older than 30 × 24 hours and no
  backup that failed its check exists
open_points.question: Which Required tests item must demonstrate the exact cutoff: a backup exactly 30 × 24 hours old is retained, one older by the smallest supported instant unit is deleted, and one cutoff reading is used for the whole deletion step?
options: Add an exact-boundary test using the representation's declared precision
Interpret Required test 2 as sufficient despite not distinguishing equality or cutoff readings
open_points.default_guess: Add an exact-boundary and single-cutoff test.

open_points.subject: A18 failed-backup invariant
open_points.text:
after a run whose deletions succeeded: no backup older than 30 × 24 hours and no
  backup that failed its check exists
open_points.question: Does “whose deletions succeeded” include deletion of a newly created backup that failed its check, or only the third-step retention deletions? The normative rules allow such a failed backup to remain under a temporary name when its deletion fails.
options: The antecedent includes every deletion attempt in the run, so the invariant does not apply when the failed backup remains
The antecedent means only third-step deletions, making the invariant contradict the permitted temporary failed backup
Rewrite the invariant to distinguish kept backups from temporary failed files
open_points.default_guess: Rewrite the invariant to say that no kept backup failed its check, while temporary failed files may remain only after a reported deletion failure.

witness.initial: A new backup fails its integrity check, deleting that backup fails, and all third-step retention deletions succeed.
events: The run leaves the failed backup under its temporary name as rule 4 permits.
A checker interprets “deletions succeeded” as the third step only; another interprets it as every deletion in the run.
outcomes: The formal invariant is violated because a failed backup file exists after successful retention deletions.
The invariant's antecedent is false because deletion of the failed backup did not succeed.
witness.observer: The factory invariant gate and the owner inspecting the backup location

open_points.subject: A19 import size enforcement
open_points.text: The import file is read as data with a size limit of 50 MB, 50 × 1024 × 1024 bytes (owner, 2026-11-11); nothing in it is executed or evaluated, and a file over the limit is refused before it is read.
open_points.question: What does “before it is read” mean for an uploaded request body, which size authority is trusted, and what happens when the declared length is absent, false, or the stream crosses the limit?
options: Reject a trustworthy declared oversize length before buffering, otherwise stream at most 50 × 1024 × 1024 bytes plus one and abort without parsing or retaining it
Require a correct Content-Length and refuse uploads without it
Read the entire upload into memory and then check its length
open_points.default_guess: Precheck a valid declared length, then enforce the same hard limit while streaming with bounded memory and never parse or retain an oversize body.

witness.initial: A client uploads a body larger than 50 × 1024 × 1024 bytes without a declared length.
events: One implementation buffers the whole body to learn its size.
Another stops after reading one byte beyond the limit and discards the upload.
outcomes: The file is refused only after the whole body has been read into memory.
The file is refused after a bounded prefix and is never parsed or retained.
witness.observer: The Registry process through memory use and the caller through connection behavior

open_points.subject: A19 and A21 file-size security evidence
open_points.text:
1. Each APPLICABLE category's decisions have their own required tests, and
   those tests pass.
open_points.question: Which A19 Required tests item demonstrates the new 50 × 1024 × 1024-byte refusal boundary and bounded pre-read behavior required by the APPLICABLE files_artifacts category?
options: Add tests for exactly-at-limit, one-byte-over, missing or false declared length, and bounded streaming
Claim the three existing rendering and round-trip tests cover file size
open_points.default_guess: Add explicit boundary and streaming-limit tests to A19 and cite A19 from files_artifacts.

open_points.subject: A21 security review status
open_points.text:
2. A change to a decision a category names reopens this review.

Performed again on 2026-11-01, after that day's changes to A01, A04, A13, A16,
A17 and A18 reopened it (rule 2): every category naming them was reviewed, and no
outcome changed
open_points.question: What are the recorded outcomes of the security review reopened by the 2026-11-11 changes to A17, A18 and A19, especially files_artifacts, injection_interpreted_input, secrets and concurrency?
options: Perform and record a new 2026-11-11 review of every category naming the changed decisions
Leave the review reopened and do not claim A21 is accepted or complete
open_points.default_guess: Perform and record the new review before closing State 2.
